title: Costs, slippage and fill assumptions

objectives.text: Apply separate adverse half-spread,slippage and per-unit fee assumptions to signed fills and reconcile a fixed-path gross/net round trip.
Stress capacity,affordability and no-fill scenarios without inferring executable size/queue priority from OHLCtouches or treating scenario costs as calibrated market truth.

blocks.markdown: Execution cost has several reference points. A quoted bid/ask spread,arrival-midpoint shortfall,decision-to-arrival move,market impact,fees and financing are not interchangeable. Avoid double counting:if the fill price is already the ask for a buy,do not add another half-spread just because a cost field exists. Slippage relative to an expected price can be favorable or adverse in real trading. Our scenario uses ONLYnonnegative adverse add-ons to an explicitly synthetic opening reference,not a statistical slippage estimate or necessarily a traded bar open.

The complete source repeats the prior engine. Buy execution=opening_reference+half_spread+adverse_slip;sell=reference-half_spread-adverse_slip. A fee_per_unit is charged on either filled side. All are integer cents per share,not basis points or percent. Costs are zero for zero fills. All opening references must exceed the sum of costs in this bounded sell-proceeds contract. This is an own symmetric stress scenario,not the broker/venue's actual fee table and not market impact calibrated to size.

steps.text: Same2-share buy110/sell120round trip gives gross gain20cents. With half-spread1,adverse slip1and fee1,buy fill112costs113including fee,so cash after buy=1000-2*113=774.
Sell fill118nets117including fee;cash ends774+2*117=1008. Difference from gross1020is12=2shares*2sides*(1spread+1slip+1fee). Marked equity at the intermediate115close is1004.

This fixed quantity/path comparison isolates drag. Costs can change affordability,which changes fills and future positions. Across different trade paths,you cannot subtract a universal cost number from an unchanged gross return and call it the simulated net strategy.

Full repeated engine so no fragment import needed. Capacity1allows only one opening buy;remainder expires. Zero capacity produces no fee/fill. These capacities are supplied opening scenarios,not future full-bar volume used at the open.

blocks.markdown: An opening target delta is capped by supplied executable capacity,affordable buy size including fees,and current sell holdings. A full-day volume participation cap would only be known after that day unless modeled as an ex-post allocation rule with declared timing;do not feed it into a point-in-time open decision unnoticed. Capacity scenarios are not queue position or fill-probability models. In a losing strategy,less execution may improve realized returns;do not promise every more conservative assumption makes every backtest PnLmonotonically lower.

An OHLCbar can show that a price level was reached without showing whether your order was already present,its queue priority,available size or the path between extremes. If both a stop and target lie within the range,their order cannot generally be inferred from OHLCalone. Use finer data or explicit conservative/alternative path scenarios,record ambiguity and retain no-fill alternatives. This capstone does not implement stop/limit/OHLCtouch fills;do not infer they were validated.

QuantConnectdocuments complete fills for pre-built backtest models and default zero slippage under its default brokerage model. Its EquityFillModelhas source-specific data/order rules,such as strict low<buy-limit/high>sell-limit for documented limit cases;these differ from inclusive touch models. Backtraderdocuments next-bar execution and configurable slip behavior. Defaults are not evidence of real liquidity or your broker's costs. Keep chosen library/config/version/data granularity and any custom overrides in the experiment manifest.

Compare no-cost/finite-cost,low/high spread,capacity0/1/full,delays,missing/stale data and different liquidation policies. Include turnover,filled/unfilled quantity,fees,exposure and terminal inventory,not only net Sharpe. Compare baselines under the SAMEdata/timing/cost rules. Historical SECinvestor education explains that execution takes time,quoted size is finite and actual price can differ;its2013page is used for these basic concepts,not current regulatory requirements or modern broker routing details.

Independent transfer:choose enough cash so fixed-path quantities do not change,and algebraically reconcile round-trip drag across several cost settings. Then deliberately cross affordability thresholds and show why the path changes. Set capacity0and prove fees zero,change only a future capacity and verify unchanged earlier prefix. Sketch two intrabar paths with identical OHLCbutdifferent stop/target order and state why neither is uniquely identified by the bar. No live order is sent.

Sources:[Backtraderslippage limits/configuration](https://www.backtrader.com/docu/slippage/slippage/),[QuantConnectfill concepts](https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/reality-modeling/trade-fills/key-concepts),[slippage concepts/defaults](https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/reality-modeling/slippage/key-concepts),[equity-specific fill rules](https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/reality-modeling/trade-fills/supported-models/equity-model),[SEC2013basic execution education](https://www.sec.gov/investor/pubs/tradexec.htm). Our symmetric cents stress and capacity interface are own design.

summary: State execution references and separate spread/slippage/fees without double counting. Capacity and affordability change trade paths;OHLCtouch does not prove queued executable volume. Stress scenarios and honest defaults are evidence of modeled assumptions,not live fill or future net-return guarantees.
